components.semantics: One node with the label, a toggled state and a tap action; the track and the label toggle it

props.name: obscure
props.default: false

props.default: off for obscure, email and url keyboards; on otherwise

components.semantics: One text field node named by the visible label, with the hint and value; invalid when errorText is set, and the error is a live region; announced read-only when readOnly. The show/hide toggle of password is a button named by the label of its next action

props.name: numeric
props.default: true

props.name: autofocus
props.default: false

components.semantics: One text field node named by label whose value is the code entered so far, never one node per cell; invalid when errorText is set, and the error is a live region

props.name: joinOrder
props.default: stable join sequence, not a list index; picks the color through AppColors.pebbleAt, wrapping after six

props.name: status
props.default: home; away draws its badge only from s44 up

props.name: isYou
props.default: false

props.name: isAdmin
props.default: false; the key badge is drawn only from s44 up

components.semantics: One image node named by semanticLabel (required, not empty), which holds the whole description (name, you, admin, away); the initials, the badges and the outline are excluded. A node of its own under a parent that does not merge; under a parent that merges its children (a MergeSemantics row) its label joins the row's. Status and role are drawn as shapes: moon badge (away), dashed outline without fill (invited), key badge (admin), inset dark ring (you). The away and admin badges are drawn only from s44 up: on s28 and s36 they are left out, so say them in semanticLabel and in the text next to the pebble. The away badge hangs at the bottom trailing corner and the admin key at the top trailing corner (the board puts the key at the bottom too, where it would cover the status badge). The pebble is always a square: exactly its side at text scale 1, growing continuously with larger text. Two initials up to MW fit at every size; wider pairs (WW) grow s28 and s36 by a pixel or two. From s44 up the side reserves room for the badge squares in every state, so pebbles of a size stay equal. On s44+ a badge may cover the tip of an accent or a descender on two-letter initials; capitals are never covered

Decorative and excluded from semantics: the dot has no label. It always sits next to the text that names the status and is never the only cue (home and busy differ only by hue), so it must never stand alone

props.name: count
props.default: AppBadge.count: the number, 99+ beyond 99

props.name: label
props.default: AppBadge.label: a short text

props.name: tone
props.default: primary for count, soft for label

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: replaces the visible text for assistive technology

components.semantics: The visible number or label is read as it is. With semanticLabel the badge is one labeled node ("3 unread") and its text is excluded. Like any semantic child it merges into a parent that merges its children (a MergeSemantics row reads the row label and the badge label as one); under a parent that does not merge it is a node of its own. Text reaches 4.5:1 on every fill; the fill carries no meaning. Callers hide the badge at 0

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: null leaves the ring out of semantics

props.name: value
props.default: null: in use with no known end, a breathing arc; 0 to 1 otherwise, clamped; must be finite

props.name: tone
props.default: primary

props.name: size
props.default: AppSizes.ring (56); grows with a large label

props.name: label
props.default: text in the middle

props.name: semanticValue
props.default: required with a value, for example 11 of 15 done

components.semantics: With a semanticLabel the ring is one node: the label names what it measures and, with a value, semanticValue says how far it is (an in-use ring never has a value); the drawing and the middle label are excluded. Null excludes the ring. Like any semantic child it merges into a parent that merges its children. The arc breathes only when animations are enabled, and stands still at full opacity otherwise. A value that is not finite is drawn as 0

props.name: ageDays
props.default: calendar days since the task was last done, counted by the app in the home's time zone; zero or less is fresh

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: null leaves the bar out of semantics: the age text beside it says it

components.semantics: Image named by semanticLabel with container: true when the label is non-empty (a node of its own under a parent that does not merge; it merges into a merging parent like any semantic child), else decorative and excluded because the age text beside it carries the meaning. It always sits beside that text in a fixed-width column and is never the only cue: the track is the sunken surface, so the end of the bar is not visible. The fill is 100, 85, 60 or 25 percent and no danger color is used

props.name: member
props.default: name, initials, joinOrder, status, isYou, isAdmin and the spoken description (semanticLabel)

props.name: subtitle
props.default: second line under the name

props.name: trailing
props.default: text at the end of the row; a status dot sits before it (none while invited)

components.semantics: One merged node, not interactive: member.semanticLabel (it names the member and says you, admin and away), then the subtitle, then the trailing text. The visible name, the pebble and the dot add nothing of their own, so nothing is said twice
notes: Layout: the pebble and the texts take up to two thirds of the row and the trailing text one third, beside each other. When the longest word of the name or the subtitle does not fit beside the pebble in its share, or the longest word of the trailing text does not fit in its third, the trailing text and its dot move under the texts and the texts take the width the pebble leaves (as the home AppTopBar does with its buttons), so no word breaks at large text. At a text scale of 1.0 in a phone column the row is laid out as before.
A small private render object lays the row out, with intrinsic and dry layout, not a LayoutBuilder, so the golden harness can measure it.
One case is left: a word wider than the whole row. It wraps by its letters, so all of it stays visible at 200% (WCAG 1.4.4); the name is never cut with an ellipsis.

The row keeps the baseline of the name, so it lines up with a neighbor in a baseline-aligned Row. The status dot sits on the middle of the first line of the trailing text. The row-long state has a long name, subtitle and trailing text, so the large text scenarios of its golden show the stacked layout.

props.name: item
props.default: id, name and the appliance glyph

props.name: inUse
props.default: in use: glyph in a breathing busy ring and a busy status text; free: glyph on a sunken tile and a muted one

props.name: statusLabel
props.default: status line under the name: the time in use, or that it is free

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: replaces the visible texts for assistive technology

components.semantics: One focusable button named by semanticLabel ("Washer, in use by Carlos, 34 minutes"), activated by tap, Enter and Space; the ring, the glyph and the visible texts add nothing of their own. Drawn at least 44 tall, hit area at least 48

props.name: room
props.default: id and name

props.name: state
props.default: home, away, occupied or free

props.name: caption
props.default: line under the name that says the state in words

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: spoken description of the whole tile

props.name: occupants
props.default: empty; drawn as s36 pebbles at the end of the footer line, wrapped under the beacons and start-aligned when they do not fit on one line

props.name: beacons
props.default: empty; pinned at the bottom start, wrapping onto more lines, each its own button

props.name: onTap
props.default: null: the tile is plain. Set: the tile is a focusable button (tap, Enter, Space), with a press layer and a 2 px ink focus ring outside the shape

components.semantics: One container node named by semanticLabel ("Bathroom, occupied by Carlos, 12 minutes"); the name, caption, lock and pebbles add nothing of their own. Without onTap it is not interactive. With onTap the same node is a focusable button with a tap action (focused only while the tile itself holds the focus). Each beacon stays its own focusable button, a child of that node, and a touch on it never reaches the tile. The state is also said by the caption, never by color or outline alone
notes: onTap is optional: without it the tile is plain, as before. With it the tile node itself is the button (label, button role, tap action and focus all on the one node) and the beacons are its children, so a screen reader meets the room first and its items inside it. The focus ring is 2 px of ink outside the shape, drawn only for the tile that holds the primary focus (not while a beacon does) and only in keyboard mode; the press layer is the surface state layer (8%) over the wall. A press that starts on a beacon is the beacon's: the tile shows no press layer for it, from the first moment to the release (a Listener around each beacon, as Material's markChildInkResponsePressed does). The node also has the focus action (not on iOS), so screen-reader focus moves the input focus. Going from no onTap to one, or back, remounts the tile and drops its focus. A parent that clips needs 2 px of room, and a neighbor must not paint over the ring.
The contract states archived and draw are not drawn: the board shows neither, and the floorplan hides archived rooms. The RoomDrawBoard organism draws the tile in its draw form.

props.name: task
props.default: id, title and ageDays (calendar days since it was last done, counted by the app in the home time zone)

props.name: subtitle
props.default: line under the title that says who did it last, when and where

props.name: logAgainSemanticLabel
props.default: name of the log button for assistive technology

components.semantics: The title and the subtitle are one merged text node; the freshness bar is excluded because the subtitle says the age. The log control is its own focusable button named by logAgainSemanticLabel ("Log Clean the kitchen again"), activated by tap, Enter and Space. The row itself is not tappable. Calm: no danger color, never who is behind

props.name: event
props.default: id, kind (visit, overnight, absence, other) and the title to show

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: spoken description with the dates the ribbon only draws by width

props.name: continuesBefore
props.default: false; flat start edge, mirrored in right-to-left

props.name: continuesAfter
props.default: false; flat end edge, mirrored in right-to-left

props.name: compact
props.default: false; the glyph alone, for a cell too narrow for a title (about 44 wide). The title is one line with an ellipsis otherwise

components.semantics: One container node named by semanticLabel ("Absence, Luis, until Fri 6 Nov"), not interactive; the glyph and the visible title add nothing of their own, and the compact form says the same with no title. The kind is told by its glyph and title, never by color alone, and a flat edge is only a shape, so the label says that the event goes on

props.name: subtitle
props.default: home only; null or empty leaves the line out

props.name: activityLabel
props.default: home only; spoken name of the bell with the unread count in words

props.name: unreadCount
props.default: home only; zero draws no badge

props.name: onActivity
props.default: home only

props.name: me
props.default: home only; the signed-in member the account pebble is drawn from (initials, joinOrder; the account is yours, so no "you" ring); required, the board has no home bar without the account button

props.name: accountLabel
props.default: home only; spoken name of the account button, the action it does ("Your account"); MemberView.semanticLabel describes the person and is not read

props.name: onAccount
props.default: home only

props.name: backLabel
props.default: pushed only; spoken name of the back button

props.name: onBack
props.default: pushed only

props.name: actionLabel
props.default: pushed only; null or empty leaves the action out

props.name: onAction
props.default: pushed only; null disables the action

components.semantics: The bar is its own semantics group, so under a Card or a list item the title stays a heading node of its own and the buttons stay buttons. The parts are read in order: the title, the subtitle, the bell, the account (the title, the back button, the action on the pushed bar). The subtitle is plain text. The bell, the account pebble, the back arrow and the action are focusable buttons named by their label props, which are never empty (the badge on the bell is merged into its button and read once, as part of activityLabel); targets are 44 drawn with a 48 hit area. The bar pads itself by the top inset of the screen (no SafeArea needed). It mirrors in right-to-left text, back arrow included, and grows with large text instead of clipping: above a text scale of 1.3 the bell and the account of the home bar drop under the title, and the badge sits beside the bell glyph, never over it
components.key: topBar.<part> (title, subtitle, activity, account, back, action)

props.name: destinations
props.default: one to four: id, icon, label, badgeCount (0 draws none) and semanticLabel of each destination

props.name: onSelected
props.default: called with the tapped index, also when it is the selected one

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: name of the navigation landmark

components.semantics: A navigation landmark named by semanticLabel. Each destination is one focusable button in a mutually exclusive group, with a selected state, named by its semanticLabel (which must contain the visible label) or else its label; a badge count is merged into that name and read once. Destinations are 52 tall and at least 48 wide. The selected one has a primary-soft plate with a 2 px primary border and ink text, so selection is not color alone. At most 4 destinations with short single-word labels, on a screen at least 360 wide (the smallest target; at 320 a word like Calendario breaks at 1.3). The one documented text scale cap of the system: labels and badge counts stop growing at 1.3, like Material NavigationBar (_kMaxLabelTextScaleFactor); the semantics keep the full label. The surface runs under the bottom inset. The order mirrors in right-to-left text

props.name: closeLabel
props.default: spoken name of the close button

props.name: titleFocusNode
props.default: null: the title is plain text. With a node it takes focus (no Tab stop) and shows the house focus ring while a keyboard user has it

props.name: namesRoute
props.default: false: with true the title heading node names the route that holds the header

components.semantics: The header is its own semantics group: under a Card or a list item the title stays a heading node of its own, read before the close button, and the button stays a button. The close button is a focusable button named by closeLabel, which is never empty, 44 drawn with a 48 hit area. The drag handle is decorative and excluded from semantics. A long title wraps and the header grows while the close button stays at the top end; the layout mirrors in right-to-left text. The title is centered on the 48 hit area of the close button (15 below the handle, board 12). With a titleFocusNode the title node is focusable and reports focused, still the heading, and the ring (2 px of ink outside the text, shown only for keyboard highlight) is drawn above it
components.key: sheet.<part> (title, close, handle, titleRing while the ring shows)
notes: titleFocusNode exists for sheets that open with focus on the title (ItemSheet). The board draws no focus state for a title, so the ring is the house one of RoomTile and the buttons. The playground forces the focused look with a node that reports focus, but the ring itself also needs keyboard highlight, so it stays off while the catalog is driven by a pointer.

namesRoute puts the route-naming flag on the title's heading node, so a sheet shown in a route (showModalBottomSheet) names that route by its title instead of repeating the title in a node of its own. It is off by default, because the flag only means something under a route scope.

props.name: actionLabel
props.default: null or empty leaves the action out

props.name: onAction
props.default: null disables the action

components.semantics: One group: the title and the body are a single text node read together, followed by the action as a focusable button named by its label (44 drawn, 48 hit area). The dashed plan motif is decorative and excluded. The copy never blames anyone. Content is centered and wraps with large text instead of clipping, so at large text it can be taller than the screen: it must sit in a scrollable screen

props.name: tone
props.default: info

props.name: actionLabel
props.default: null or empty leaves the action out

props.name: onAction
props.default: null disables the action

props.name: visible
props.default: true; changing it plays the enter or the exit over motion.snackbar, at once under disableAnimations

components.semantics: A live region named by message (never empty), announced once when it appears; the glyph and the text are excluded. The action is a focusable button named by actionLabel after the message (44 drawn, 48 hit area, light focus ring, an overlay of the soft primary, a dimmer disabled state); an action wider than a quarter of the bar moves under the message, end-aligned, as Material does, so the message keeps its words whole at 2.0. The tone is a glyph (check or circled exclamation mark), never color alone and never a danger color. No timer: the app decides when to show and dismiss it by flipping visible. After the exit the bar takes no space and leaves the semantics and the focus order, and while it leaves the action cannot take focus

props.name: entry
props.default: id, glyph (icon), tone (neutral or busy), text (a list of runs, each with a strong flag, in the word order of the language) and meta (muted line under it)

props.name: unread
props.default: unread: a dot at the end of the row

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: spoken description of the entry: it says whether the entry is unread ("Unread. Carlos finished your washer") and holds the visible text in the same words (WCAG 2.5.3)

components.semantics: One focusable button named by semanticLabel, activated by tap, Enter and Space. The tile, the texts and the unread dot add nothing of their own, so nothing is said twice. Unread is a shape (the dot) and is in the spoken label, never color alone. Calm: busy is amber, never a danger color, never who is behind
notes: Board gaps: the tile glyph is 18 (size.glyph-lg) where the board draws 20, and the tile corner is radius.sm (10) where the board draws 12.

Board gaps: the row is 64 tall with 12 of padding where the board draws 68 with 14, and the 2 px between the message and the meta line is not drawn. None of 14, 2 or 68 is a token, and a row that is 64 like the member row keeps the list rhythm.
The line is a list of runs (ActivityText with a strong flag) so the bold part can sit anywhere, as in 'Room draw: you got Bedroom 1'.

props.name: value
props.default: home or away: the selected side

props.name: onChanged
props.default: called with the other side only; choosing the selected side does nothing

props.name: homeLabel
props.default: label of the home side

props.name: awayLabel
props.default: label of the away side

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: name of the group for assistive technology ("Your presence")

components.semantics: A radio group named by semanticLabel with two toggle buttons (homeLabel, awayLabel), exactly one checked and in a mutually exclusive group, each focusable and activated by tap, Enter and Space. The glyphs and the second drawing of each face (see notes) add nothing. The selected side is the only one under a filled thumb (3:1 against the track) and both sides have their own glyph and label, so the state is never color alone
notes: Board gaps: the board builds the sides from two AppButtons with a fill each, but the away side is filled with presence-away and AppButton has no variant for it, so the sides are Material TextButtons under one filled thumb that slides.

Board gaps: the track gets a 1 px outline border the board does not draw, so it keeps 3:1 against the page and a card. With it the sides are 54 tall where the board draws 56 (64 minus 4 and 4), and their corner is 11 where the board draws 12.

While the thumb slides every label and glyph is drawn twice, in the muted ink clipped to what is outside the thumb and in the on-color clipped to the thumb, so no color is blended and every pixel reads on every frame. At rest each face is drawn once. The second drawing is excluded from semantics, pointer and focus. The thumb jumps when animations are off. Each face sets its own text style, so a line limit, an italic or an underline around the switch does not change a label while the thumb slides.
The contract names a Presence type: it is a new two-value enum (home, away) because MemberStatus also has invited.

props.name: label
props.default: visible label of the ready button ("Who's home?"), which names it

props.name: onKnock
props.default: called by a tap while the button is ready

props.name: cooldown
props.default: null: ready. Set: inert, with the share of the wait left (remaining, 0 to 1, never NaN), a label ("Asked"), the time left ("11 min") and the spoken sentence (semanticLabel)

components.semantics: One node in both states, never replaced: a button, focusable, with a focus action and a focused flag. Ready: enabled, named by label, a tap calls onKnock. Cooldown: the same node marked disabled, without the tap action, named by cooldown.semanticLabel ("Asked who's home. You can ask again in 11 minutes"). The visible texts, the ring and Material's own node add nothing. The Material button is the same widget in both states and stays focusable and inert in the wait, so keyboard focus stays on it when the wait starts and the next Tab goes to the next control. The wait is told by words and a ring, never color alone. Calm: no danger color, no blame
notes: The contract lists availableAt: DateTime? and now: DateTime. The design system keeps no clock and no dates, so the app counts the wait and passes KnockCooldown (remaining share, label, time left, spoken sentence) instead.
Board gaps: the glyph is 18 (size.glyph-lg) where the board draws 20, and the 2 px between the ring and the two lines of text, and between them, is not drawn (there is no 2 px token).
Board gaps: the ring is AppProgressRing at 24 with its 4 px stroke where the board draws a 2.5 px one, and its track has the same color as the sunken fill, so only the arc shows.

The semantics node is the same one before and after the wait starts (a test compares its id and checks it is still focused), so a screen reader keeps its cursor. How a given screen reader announces the change of name and enabled state is not verified on a device.

props.name: code
props.default: the code as shown, already grouped by the app ("4829 1736"); it wraps at the spaces and always reads left to right

props.name: label
props.default: caption over the code, which also names it for assistive technology ("Your personal code")

props.name: copyLabel
props.default: label of the copy button

props.name: copiedLabel
props.default: label of the copy button once copied

props.name: shareLabel
props.default: label of the share button

props.name: copied
props.default: false; true shows copiedLabel and a check on the copy button. The app must announce the copy too, for example with an AppSnackbar

props.name: onCopy
props.default: the app does the clipboard

props.name: onShare
props.default: the app does the share sheet

components.semantics: The code is one node named by label whose value is the code spelled out character by character; the visible texts add nothing. Copy and share are their own focusable buttons named by their visible labels, activated by tap, Enter and Space. The card is not interactive. Copied is a label and a check, never color alone
notes: The contract lists code, onCopy and onShare. Every visible string is a prop, so label, copyLabel, copiedLabel and shareLabel are added, with copied for the state the app sets.

Board gaps: the board's buttons have no glyphs and these show the copy, check and share ones; the buttons are AppButton secondary, 52 tall with a radius of 16, where the board draws 48 and 12; the card radius is radius.sm (10) where the board draws 12.
The buttons stack at large text, which the board's two-column grid cannot. The dashed edge is decoration in the hairline color, as on RoomTile, because the card is not a control.
A code that is not grouped (eight digits with no space) is one word: at 2.0x it can be wider than the card and is cut inside the word. The app groups it.

props.name: view
props.default: unread and earlier entries (each an ActivityEntry: an ActivityView and its spoken label, unread by the list it sits in), unreadCount (the number the badge shows, at least the unread entries listed, and the app's spoken heading must use the same number), unreadPrefix (the word put before the spoken label of every unread entry), the two headings, the spoken first heading with the count in words, the label of the mark-all action, and the title and body of the empty state

props.name: onOpen
props.default: called with the id of the tapped entry

props.name: onMarkAllRead
props.default: called by the ghost action beside the first heading, which only shows while something is unread

components.semantics: A container holding one container per group. Each group is a heading node (the first says the count in words, 'New, 2 unread'), then a list node whose items are single button nodes named by the entry's spoken label, with the view's unreadPrefix before it for the unread ones only, so nothing is said twice; the mark-all action is a button named by its visible label. The badge, the dividers and the card add nothing. A group with no entries is left out and both empty is an AppEmptyState with no action. Unread is the dot, the count and the spoken prefix, never color alone. The groups are keyed, so focus and the node of a row survive the first group appearing or leaving, and when the action is pressed with focus on it and the app takes it away, even after an await, focus moves to the second heading (only if that heading is mounted, and not if focus went elsewhere in between; a rebuild with the same view does not cancel it), and that heading draws a 2 px ink ring around itself while it has focus (it paints nothing otherwise). Calm: no danger color, never who is behind. ActivityList.sliver has the same tree
components.key: activity.list, in both the list and the empty state, and a sliver in the sliver form, as is activity.card.<unread|earlier> there, so getRect does not apply to them (also activity.group.<unread|earlier> on a heading, activity.card.<unread|earlier>, activity.markAllRead, activity.empty, activity.item.<entryId> on the list item of a row, and activity.<entryId> on the row)
notes: The contract lists ActivityListView(unread, earlier) and the board draws bare 'New' and 'Earlier' headings. The contract also asks for the unread count in the header and for onMarkAllRead, which the board does not place: the count is an AppBadge beside the first heading and the action is a ghost AppButton at the end of its line, wrapping under the heading at large text. Where the action sits is a design choice to confirm with the board's owner.

Board gaps: the rows are ActivityRow (64 tall, 40 tile, radius.sm) where the board draws a 36 tile at 12 of padding. The card has radius.md (16) as the board and 4 of padding all round (spacing.xs) so the focus ring of a row, drawn outside its shape, is not cut, which the board does not have. The gap between a heading, its card and the next group is 8 as on the board. The Earlier card is filled with the surface like the New one, where the board draws it with a border only. The dividers are 1 px hairlines in the line color between rows (the flat elevation token, which wins over the board's sunken color), with no inset.

Unread is not a field of the entry: it is the list the entry sits in, so an entry cannot be both, and the list adds unreadPrefix to the spoken label of the unread ones, so an earlier entry can never say it. The badge counts unreadCount, which is more than the entries listed when the app pages. The ids of both lists must be unique, an assert checks it in debug builds.

Two forms, one class. ActivityList(...) is a box: a plain column that builds every row it gets (200 rows took 2.2 s, 3000 took 25.6 s), for a short list inside a ListView, a SingleChildScrollView or a SliverToBoxAdapter. ActivityList.sliver(...) is a static method that returns the sliver form (SliverMainAxisGroup, DecoratedSliver and SliverList.builder with the same data, callbacks, looks and semantics), for the 90 days feed directly in a CustomScrollView: with 1000 entries it builds about 7 rows at the top and 8 at the end. It is a method and not a constructor because a sliver cannot be a box widget, and it adds no class to the manifest. The sliver looks the same, so it has no use case of its own.

The heading (a 13/600 muted text that may carry a badge and an action) is a private copy here and in PresencePanel, because an organism may not import another. Planned follow-up: a SectionHeader molecule, then both organisms use it.
Semantics use Flutter's list and listItem roles on the card and its items. How a given screen reader announces them is not verified on a device.

props.name: view
props.default: home and away groups and an optional invited group (each a PresenceGroup: a title, PresenceEntry rows with a MemberView, subtitle and trailing text, and an optional label for when it is empty), and the broadcast (PresenceBroadcast: the label of the button, the optional KnockCooldown, an optional message and hint)

props.name: onKnock
props.default: called by a tap on the button while the home can be asked

components.semantics: A container holding one container per group and one for the asking part. Each group is a heading node, then a list node whose items each hold one merged MemberRow node (the member's spoken label, then the subtitle and the trailing text, so the visible name, the pebble and the dot add nothing). The asking part is the KnockButton's single node (ready: a button named by its label; waiting: the same node disabled and named by the cooldown sentence), then one merged node with the message and the hint. A group with no members says its empty label in place of the list, and one with neither is left out. Away and invited are told by words, a dot or ring and the pebble, never color alone. Calm: it says where people are, never who is behind or who did not answer
components.key: presence.panel (also presence.section.<home|away|invited>, presence.card.<home|away|invited>, presence.empty.<home|away|invited>, presence.item.<memberId> on the list item of a member, member.<memberId> on the row, presence.broadcast, presence.message, presence.hint, and presence.knock on the button)
notes: The brief for this slice named PresenceSwitch for the person using the app. The board and the contract do not: the contract is PresenceView and onKnock with no callback for a change of presence, and the board draws only the members and the knock card. The panel therefore has no switch: the person is one of the members (MemberView.isYou) and the app places the PresenceSwitch molecule on its own screen.

The contract lists PresenceView(home, away, invited, broadcast). The board draws no headings and only a home and an away member, while the contract says the sections are headers: each group has a title shown as a heading. The everyone-away state has no drawing on the board: it is the home group with no members and an empty label in place of its rows.

Board gaps: the board draws a 48 ring with the minutes inside and the words beside it, and the panel uses the KnockButton molecule (a 24 ring with 'Asked' and the time left, inside its own sunken button) with the message and the hint beside it, wrapping under it at large text. Rows are MemberRow (64 tall) where the board draws 60, and a 1 px hairline in the line color (the flat elevation token) separates rows, with no inset. The gap between cards is 12 as on the board; the board draws no headings, so the heading and its 8 of space are new.

The words beside the button are a Wrap child, not an expanded one, so they sit beside the button only when they fit whole and otherwise go under it: a long word is never cut. The button and the words sit in a card with 12 of padding (spacing.sm plus spacing.xs, as in ActivityRow).
The heading (a 13/600 muted text) is a private copy here and in ActivityList, because an organism may not import another. Planned follow-up: a SectionHeader molecule, then both organisms use it.

It is a plain column, not a scrollable: put it in the scrollable of the screen. A member must be in one group only and in the group of their status (home, away or invited), and asserts check both in debug builds. The groups are keyed, so a member's node survives another group gaining its first member.
Semantics use Flutter's list and listItem roles on the card and its items. How a given screen reader announces them, and the change of the button from ready to waiting, is not verified on a device.

props.name: view
props.default: the seven days (each a CalendarStripDay: its YYYY-MM-DD date, the visible weekday and number, and its spoken label), the events that touch them (each a CalendarStripEvent: a CalendarEventView, its first and last day as YYYY-MM-DD strings, which may lie outside the week, and its spoken label) and which date is today, or null

props.name: onDayTap
props.default: called with the YYYY-MM-DD date of the tapped day

props.name: onEventTap
props.default: called with the id of the tapped event

components.semantics: A container holding one button per day and, when there are events, a list node with one list item per event. A day is a single button node named by the app's spoken label of the day followed by the spoken label of every event that covers it, so a day reads its events; the visible weekday and number add nothing of their own. An event is a single button node named by its spoken label, which contains the visible title (label in name); its glyph tile and title add nothing. The ribbons of the band under the days are decorative and say nothing. Today is the filled cell and the app's spoken label, never color alone; the kind of an event is its glyph and its title, never color alone. Calm: no danger color, never who is behind
components.key: calendar.strip (also calendar.day.<yyyy-mm-dd> on the button of a day, calendar.events on the list, calendar.event.<eventId> on the button of an event, calendar.ribbon.<eventId>.<yyyy-mm-dd> on the piece of a ribbon, and event.<eventId> on the EventRibbon inside a piece and a button)
notes: The contract lists CalendarStripView(days: List<LocalDate>, events, today). The design system has no LocalDate: dates are YYYY-MM-DD strings in the home's zone (the board's rule) that the strip only compares as strings, which order like the dates they spell. Every visible text is a prop, so a day carries its weekday, its number and its spoken label, and an event its first day, its last day and its spoken label. The ids of the events are the keys of their rows and the dates of the days the keys of the cells, and asserts check that both are unique, the dates in order and the week seven days long in debug builds. An event that touches none of the days is left out.

Board gap, the title: the board writes the title of an event on a ribbon that spans its days. EventRibbon cuts its title with an ellipsis, and a ribbon over 44 wide columns cannot hold a title at 200% text, which WCAG 1.4.4 does not allow us to lose. So the band under the days draws one compact ribbon (the glyph on the fill of the kind) on each day an event covers, the pieces joining where the event goes on and keeping a flat edge where it goes on past the week, and the whole title is in a list under the band, wrapped and never cut. The band is decoration (it says nothing to assistive technology); the list rows are the buttons of the events, so onEventTap is reachable at 48 tall, which a 28 tall ribbon is not.

Board gap, the cells: the board draws a 12 padding, a 4 gap between columns and a 44 tall day row, which makes a column about 40 wide in a phone. A day is a button and needs at least 44 drawn and 48 of hit area, so the card pads only 4 at the sides, the columns have no gap, a day is 48 tall, and a column is 44.3 wide at 320 and 45.4 at 328. The button of a day is 48 wide, so it spills over its column by up to 2 px on each side and overlaps its neighbors, and its semantics node is 48 wide. The touch area is the column, 44.3 px at 320 wide and at least 48 from 346 wide: a tap in the part of the button that spills over the next column goes to the next day, and the tap-target guideline passes on the node rect only. Material's date picker has the same 7 columns in 328.

Board gap, large text: seven columns cannot hold a weekday at 200% text (Wed is 49 wide at 11 px and 2.0, and the board's day cell is 44). When the longest word of a day cell does not fit its share of the width, the days move to two rows of four and three, and the ribbons go with their days. The board does not draw this. At 1.0 to 1.5 in a 320 column the strip is one row.

Board gap, lanes: events are placed in the first row of the band they do not overlap, in the order the app gives them. The board draws the one day events on the second row; here the overnight stay of Saturday goes on the first row beside the absence, because it does not overlap it. Two events side by side keep 4 between them (a 2 inset on each rounded end).

Today is the filled primary cell with on-primary text, as on the board, which draws no other cue: the fill is a shape and a luminance step and the spoken label carries it, so the app must say 'today' in the label of that day. It is not color alone, but it is the only visible cue.

A day reads the spoken labels of the events that cover it (the contract's 'each day reads its events'), and the event row says the same label again to be activated, so an event is said once on each day it covers and once in the list. A label must contain its visible texts (the weekday and the number for a day, the title for an event); asserts check it in debug builds.
The empty week has no text of its own: neither the board nor the contract draws one. It is the seven days alone.

The weekday is the short form the app chooses and is never cut by an ellipsis. A weekday wider than the whole row still wraps by its letters, as any text does. How a screen reader announces the list, the days and a change of today is not verified on a device.

props.name: view
props.default: the query typed so far, the suggestions found for it (each a TaskSuggestion: id, title and an optional subtitle), the rooms (RoomView) and items (ItemView) a task can be tied to, which of them is linked (a TaskTarget: its kind and id) or null, the label and the optional hint and helper text of the field, the spoken names of the list and of the chips, the label of the button, whether it is submitting and the spoken value of the button while it waits

props.name: onQuery
props.default: called with the text of the field every time it changes

props.name: onPick
props.default: called with the id of the chosen suggestion

props.name: onLink
props.default: called with the room or item of the pressed chip, or with null when the chip that is on is pressed again

props.name: onSubmit
props.default: called by the button, or the keyboard's done key, with a TaskSubmission (the name in the field without the spaces around it, and the link); only while the field has more than spaces and the view is not submitting

components.semantics: A form container. The field is AppTextField, named by the visible label. The suggestions, when there are any, are a list node named by suggestionsLabel with one list item per suggestion, each a single button node whose name is its title and subtitle together, so the spoken name is the visible text (label in name). The chips are a container named by targetsLabel; each is an AppChip button named by its label, selected when linked, with the check and the border as the visible cue, and an item is dashed where a room is solid. The button is an AppButton named by its label, disabled until the name has more than spaces; while submitting it stays the same focusable button, ignores every activation and adds loadingLabel as its value in a live region, the field is read-only and the suggestions and chips are disabled. Calm: no danger color, never who is behind
components.key: tasks.composer (also tasks.composer.field, tasks.composer.suggestions, tasks.composer.suggestion.<taskId> on the button of a suggestion, tasks.composer.targets, tasks.composer.room.<roomId> and tasks.composer.item.<itemId> on a chip, and tasks.composer.submit)
notes: The contract lists TaskComposerView(query, suggestions, rooms, items, linked). The design system has no types for a suggestion or a link, so TaskSuggestion carries an id, a title and a subtitle, rooms and items are the RoomView and ItemView the floorplan already uses (the icon of an item is not drawn), and the link is a TaskTarget with a kind and an id, because a room and an item may share an id. Every visible text is a prop: the label, the hint, the helper text, the label of the button, and the spoken names of the list and the chips, which the board does not draw. The ids of each list are the keys of its rows and chips, and asserts check that each list has unique ids in debug builds.

The contract lists onSubmit(name, note, target) but the board draws no field for a note, so there is none: onSubmit gives a TaskSubmission with the name and the target, a value object so that a note can be added later without changing the signature. A note is a follow-up for the board's owner to confirm. onLink is told by the contract as onLink(target) and does not say how a link is removed: pressing the chip that is on calls onLink(null).

Board gap, the field: the board draws one box with the 2 px primary border that holds the text input and, under it, the one suggestion on the sunken color. AppTextField is a field with its own label above, its own border and focus ring, so the field and the suggestions are two things here: the field, then a sunken card with a hairline between suggestions, each at least 52 tall as on the board (a suggestion is a button with its title in 15/600 and its subtitle in 12 muted). The board shows one suggestion, and the composer shows as many as the app sends, in its order.

Board gaps, the states: the board draws only the match (the typed name, a suggestion that says it is the same task as before, the chosen room and the button). The other four are drawn from the contract's names: empty is an empty field with a hint and the button disabled, typing is a name still being typed with the suggestions found so far, new task is a name with no suggestion and a helper line under the field that the app passes to say it is new (the board draws no text for it), and submitting is the match with the button waiting, the field read-only and the rest disabled. Which of them a view is, is decided by what the app passes in.

The rule of the board, that matching ignores case and extra spaces like the backend catalog, is the app's, because the composer takes the suggestions already found. The composer also applies it to what it draws: a suggestion whose title is the same as an earlier one by that rule is left out, so the same task is never offered twice.

The field shows the text the person typed. The texts sent through onQuery are remembered until the app answers, and a query that comes back as one of them, even late and after more was typed, is an echo and leaves the field, its caret and its composing region alone. The field is replaced only by a query the app changed by itself (a picked suggestion, an emptied form after logging), caret at the end. The button and the done key log the text of the field, not the query of the view, so a key the app has not heard yet is not lost; the button is enabled from the field too. A debug assert checks that the linked target is one of the rooms or items.

The words put the chips under the field and the button last, as the board does, with 16 of padding and 12 between the parts. The chips are 44 tall AppChips that wrap onto more lines, so at large text a long name wraps inside its chip and the chips wrap under each other.

The list is announced as a list by its role and its name, and not as a live region: announcing every change of the suggestions would speak on every key. How a screen reader announces the list, the form role and the change of the button from ready to waiting is not verified on a device.

props.name: view
props.default: the rooms (each a FloorplanRoom: a RoomView, its kind bedroom or common, its RoomTileState, the caption and the spoken label of the tile, the occupants as MemberView, the items pinned to it as FloorplanItem (an ItemView, whether it is in use, its status line and its spoken label) and whether it is archived), the members who are out (each a FloorplanAbsence: a MemberView and an optional label such as 'until Fri'), the heading of the away tray, the title and body of the empty state, the spoken name of the loading state and whether it is loading

props.name: onRoomTap
props.default: called with the id of the tapped room

props.name: onItemTap
props.default: called with the id of the tapped item (the beacon)

props.name: onMemberTap
props.default: called with the id of the tapped member of the away tray

components.semantics: A container holding the plan, a list node whose list items each hold one room, and then the away tray. A room is a single focusable button node named by its spoken label ("Ana's room, Ana is home, 3 hours"), which contains the visible name; its caption, name and pebbles add nothing of their own. A beacon is its own button node, a child of its room, named by its spoken label ("Washer, in use by Carlos, 34 minutes"); a touch on it never reaches the room. The tray is a group named by its heading, holding one button for each absent member named by the spoken label of the member and then the words beside the pebble. Loading is one ring node named by the loading label and nothing else; empty is the empty state. The state of a room is said by its caption and label, and of a member in the tray by words and a moon, never by color alone. Calm: busy is amber, no danger color, never who is behind
components.key: floorplan.map (also floorplan.room.<roomId> on the node of a tile, floorplan.item.<itemId> on a beacon, floorplan.awayTray on the tray, floorplan.member.<accountId> on the button of an absent member, roomTile.pebble.<memberId> on an occupant)
notes: AwayTray is a private part of FloorplanMap, not an organism of its own. The board draws it inside the map card, gives it the key floorplan.awayTray in the map's key list and lists onMemberTap among the map's events, and an organism may not import another one, so a separate organism would make the app compose the two and place the tray by hand. If the app ever wants the tray on its own screen, promote it then.

The board lists the map's data as FloorplanView(rooms, members, items, usages, absences, meId, now). The design system keeps no clock and no snapshot, and every word is the app's, so the app hands over rooms that are already worded: each FloorplanRoom carries its state, caption, spoken label, occupants and its items, each FloorplanItem whether it is in use and its status line, and each FloorplanAbsence its label ('until Fri'). usages and now become those words and durations, meId becomes MemberView.isYou, and members and items are inside the rooms. Rooms that are archived have a flag and are not drawn, with their items. The ids of the rooms, of the items across every room and of the members of the tray are the keys, and asserts check that they are unique, and that the spoken label of a room and of an item contains its visible name (label in name), in debug builds. A tray button is named by the spoken label of the member and the words beside the pebble, so it contains them by construction.

Board gap, the layout rule: the board's picture puts the bathroom in the top row between two bedrooms, while its written rule says bedrooms fill the top and bottom rows and common areas the middle. The written rule is what is built: the bedrooms are split between a top section (the larger half when odd) and a bottom one, the common areas fill the middle, all in the order the app gives them. With the board's data the top is Ana and Luis, the middle the bathroom, the kitchen and the living room, and the bottom Carlos and Bedroom 4. A row holds at most three tiles that share the width equally, which is not the board's six column grid with spans of two and three.

Board gap, narrow columns and large text: the board's cells are about 90 wide in a phone, which cannot hold a word of a room at 200% text or the beacon of the kitchen without cutting it (WCAG 1.4.4). A row therefore takes fewer tiles when the longest word of a tile (or a beacon, or 48) does not fit its share, and the tiles of the section move to rows of two and then one, spread as evenly as possible. At 320 wide the board's data is already two across for the common areas at 1.0, and one column at 200%. A small render object with intrinsic and dry layout does it, not a LayoutBuilder.

Board gap, sizes: the board's rows are 100, 104 and 84 tall, with a 6 gap and 6 of padding. There is no token for the height of a plan row, so a row is as tall as its tallest tile and at least AppSizes.rowTall (72), the gap is spacing.sm (8) and the paddings are 8. The gap holds the 2 px focus ring of a tile and the 4 px glow of its neighbor side by side, so no tile paints over the ring of another and nothing has to paint last (CalendarStrip needs paintLast because its columns have no gap). The board's dotted floor texture is decoration and is left out. The card has the surface fill and a hairline edge, the plan sits on the page color.

A room tile is tappable and holds buttons. RoomTile gained an optional onTap for this (in the commit before this one): the one node of the tile is the button and the beacons are its children, so a screen reader meets the room first and the items inside it, and a touch on a beacon is the beacon's. The occupants drawn in a tile are not buttons: a touch on a pebble is a touch on the room. Only the members of the tray are tapped as members.

Board gap, 'the map is followed by the same facts as a list for screen readers': the plan is exposed as a list (list and listItem roles) whose items are the rooms, so the facts are the room nodes themselves, in reading order. A second hidden list repeating them would make a screen reader read every room twice, so none is drawn. How a screen reader announces the list, the rooms and the beacons inside them, and the order of focus (a tile, then its beacons, then the next tile) is not verified on a device.

Board gap, the tray: the board draws a moon and 'Away', then a pebble with only its initial and 'until Fri'. Each absent member is a button (48 by 48 at least, so it can open the member) named by the spoken label of the member followed by the words, which are the only visible text: the name is not drawn, as on the board. The tray wraps onto more lines when the members do not fit. It is left out when nobody is away, and the room of an absent member still shows as away in the plan.

Board gap, loading and empty: the board draws neither. Loading is the in-use ring (it breathes, and stands still when animations are off) named by the loading label, with nothing else; the plan with no room that is not archived is the empty state of the design system, and the tray is not drawn with it. Both words are props.

Touch targets: every tile is at least 48 by 48 and the whole wall is its target; a beacon is 44 drawn with a 48 hit area, inside its tile, so the tile answers everywhere else. Nothing in the geometry makes 48 impossible: at 320 wide and 200% text the tiles are a single column. A tile's wall is the hit area, so the glow and the focus ring outside it are not.

props.name: view
props.default: the item (ItemView, which keys the sheet), the mode (start, finish, nudge, remind or cooldown), who is using it (ItemUsage: a MemberView and the worded subtitle, null exactly for a start), the title, the optional message (required for a cooldown), the label of the confirm button and the spoken label of the close button

props.name: onConfirm
props.default: called by the confirm button, which is disabled in cooldown

props.name: onClose
props.default: called by the close button and by the Escape key

components.semantics: A container holding the SheetHeader (the title is a heading that names the route that shows the sheet, so the route announces the question once, and takes the initial focus, then the close button), the usage as one merged MemberRow node (the member's spoken label, then the subtitle), the message as a text and the confirm button, a single button node named by its visible label (disabled in cooldown, so it is announced as unavailable and the message before it says why). Focus starts on the title once the sheet is laid out, only if the title is still attached; a rebuild never asks for it again, and a view that disables the button while it has focus moves focus to the title instead of dropping it to the route. Escape closes. Nothing is told by color alone: the wait is in the message and the disabled button
components.key: itemSheet.<itemId> (also sheet.title, sheet.close and sheet.handle from the header, member.<memberId> on the usage row, itemSheet.message and itemSheet.confirm)
notes: The board's contract is ItemSheetView(item, usage, mode, nudgeAvailableAt). The design system has no clock, so there is no instant: the app words the wait into the message and sends the mode cooldown, as FloorplanMap and PresencePanel do. The view carries the visible words (title, message, confirm and close labels) because the app owns localization. nudgeAvailableAt is therefore not a prop, and a cooldown without a message is rejected in debug builds.

Board gap, the modes: the board draws only one sheet, a nudge ("Ask Carlos to free the washer?", Carlos started it 34 min ago, "You can ask the same person once every 15 minutes.", Send request) and lists "start | finish | nudge | remind" in its caption, with cooldown added by the contract. It says nothing of what start, finish and remind look like. They are built as the same sheet with other words: start has no usage (the item is free), finish, nudge and remind each have the person using the item, and cooldown is a nudge or a remind whose button waits. The business rules say the user of an item can be asked to free it or reminded with a cooldown, and that anyone can finish a use, which is what finish, nudge and remind follow. The mode decides which parts must be there and whether the button waits; the wording is the app's. The sheet does not tell a nudge from a remind visually.

Board gap, the usage row: the board's row has the item name (Washer) as the title and Carlos' pebble, with the usage text as the subtitle. MemberRow names the member, so the row shows the member's name with the subtitle the app words ("Started 34 min ago"), and the item is named by the title. ItemView.name and icon are not drawn; the item only keys the sheet. The row sits on the sunken card color with 12 of side padding and is 64 tall (board 60).

Board gap, the surface: the board draws the sheet with 24 top corners, a 12 radius at the bottom and the sheet shadow, over a page. The sheet here has 24 top corners only (it is anchored to the bottom of the screen by its route) and adds the bottom safe-area inset (MediaQuery.padding, so an ancestor SafeArea is not doubled) under the button. The message is the body style (15/22) where the board draws 13/20, because no 13/20 regular text token exists. Spacing is 12 between the parts as on the board.

SheetHeader gained an optional titleFocusNode for this (in the commit before this one): the title is the starting point of focus, so it is focusable without a Tab stop and has the house focus ring for keyboard users. The next Tab reaches the close button, then the confirm button.

Hosting: show it with showModalBottomSheet(isScrollControlled: true, backgroundColor: Colors.transparent, ...). The sheet draws its own surface, the route supplies the barrier, the focus scope and the route semantics (one scopesRoute node), and the title heading names that route (SheetHeader.namesRoute), so the title is not said twice. On Android the route also carries Flutter's own 'Dialog' label on its node; which name a given screen reader prefers is not verified on a device. A new item id mounts the content again (focus falls back through the scope's history, to the title once it was there).

Scrolling: the header stays pinned and the body (the person, the message, the button) scrolls inside the sheet when the height is bounded, which is the case in showModalBottomSheet. When the header alone would take more than half of the bounded height (the default route caps a sheet at 9/16 of the screen, so at 2.0 text on 320 by 568 the title fills it), the header stops being pinned and scrolls together with the body, so the button is still reached; at exactly half it is still pinned. The outer scroll is a Scrollable around the private render object, which is a viewport (RenderAbstractViewport) so ensureVisible and screen-reader focus scroll it. A small private render object gives the body what the header leaves of a bounded height and is a plain column when the height is unbounded (a column with a flex child asserts there), so intrinsic sizes and dry layout still work for the golden harness. onClose is called by the close button and by Escape while focus is inside the sheet; the barrier, a drag down and the route's DismissIntent bypass it, so the app must treat the route's pop result as a close too.

Nudge message: the backend's nudge endpoint takes an optional message of up to 280 characters, and the sheet has no field for it because the board draws none. A text field (AppTextField) in the body and an onConfirm that carries the text is a follow-up. Remind follows the contract's REMINDER meaning (the washer finished hours ago); nudge, remind and cooldown cannot target the user's own use (the backend answers HOME_CANNOT_NUDGE_SELF), and ItemSheet asserts it in debug builds (ItemSheetView stays const, which cannot read the member).
